data.narrative:
KP Labs is a Series A-stage frontier aerospace company founded by Krzysztof Pacan. The valuation universe comprises 13 peers across Space & Aerospace: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Two standard valuation methods were tested. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 11 same-sector peers exist, none of the targeted subsets (same stage, adjacent stage, similar-tier) yielded the minimum 3 datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because KP Labs' revenue is not disclosed; the broader Space & Aerospace sector trades at a 23.9x median P/S across the 6 public comparables, but this multiple cannot be applied without a revenue figure. Both methods encountered constraints endemic to early-stage private aerospace—sparse same-stage private data and revenue opacity.

The analysis does not produce a quantitative valuation range. Without applicable triangulation methods, no sober estimate can be synthesized from the available data. A credible valuation would require either: (i) disclosure or estimation of KP Labs' revenue and gross margin profile; (ii) access to terms from recent private fundraises among the listed peers; or (iii) expansion beyond sector peers to broader frontier-tech or deep-tech Series A cohorts. Key uncertainty centers on whether comparable private aerospace firms at identical stage have raised at multiples anchored to public P/S multiples or at steeper discounts reflecting execution and market risk.
